name: EPA Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) reporting facilities
publisher: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Toxics Release Inventory Program
basic_page_phrases: Each "Basic" data file contains the 100 most-used data fields from the TRI Reporting Form R and Form A Certification Statement.
facilities may revise previous years' TRI submissions if necessary, and any such changes will be reflected in these files.
data contained in these files may differ from data used to construct the annual TRI National Analysis.
processed_as_of_pattern: Includes reporting forms processed as of:\s*([A-Z][a-z]+ \d{1,2}, \d{4})
documentation_phrases: The unique TRI facility identification number assigned to each facility for TRI reporting purposes.
the TRI Facility ID identifies a specific geographical location which is also identified by the latitude and longitude of that location.
Unique identification number assigned to each TRI form submission.
The latitude value that best represents the facility according to EPA's Facility Registry System (FRS).
The Basic Data file record will contain zeroes for all release and other management quantities from a Form A.
Indicates whether the facility submitted a Reporting Form R or Form A Certification Statement.
Allowed values: NAD27, NAD83 and WGS84.
documentation_note: EPA's Basic Data Files documentation PDF (August 2024) says 'Updated for RY 2023'. It was the documentation linked from the basic-files page on 2026-11-14. The RY2024 file header is reviewed exactly below (it spells the facility ID column 'TRIFD').
report_level_note: Industry sector and NAICS codes are carried on each chemical form. In the RY2024 file 41 facilities have forms in more than one TRI industry sector (61 with more than one primary NAICS), so a facility's industry is the set of sectors on its forms; no single sector is chosen.
chemical_name_note: One TRI chemical ID can carry different published names (for example 'Lead compounds' and 'Lead  And Lead Compounds' when the elemental metal is included on a combined form). CHIP lists every published name; it does not pick one.

generic_chemical_ids.MIXTURE: EPA's generic identity 'Mixture': the chemical was reported as a mixture component without a specific identity.
generic_chemical_ids.TRD SECRT: EPA's sanitized identity 'Trade Secret': the chemical identity was claimed as a trade secret.

vocabulary_note: HORIZONTAL DATUM is blank on every RY2024 row (documented allowed values NAD27, NAD83, WGS84). Any non-blank datum would need a reviewed transformation decision and holds the candidate.
industry_sector_note: TRI industry sectors are EPA's published 'INDUSTRY SECTOR CODE' / 'INDUSTRY SECTOR' pairs (NAICS-based groupings used by the TRI Program). The list is the reviewed RY2024 vocabulary; any other code or label holds the candidate.

detail_link.label: EPA Facility Registry Service record for this TRI facility ID
detail_link.verification: Verified 2026-11-14 for RY2024 IDs 71730NVRNM309AM, 43920VNRLL1250S, 9692WYGPWRMARIN, 0096WPMNRG1922A, 77643WSTMNHWY73 and 2871WCRLNR1186S (no FRS ID in the file): each page names the facility and its FRS registry ID; a made-up ID returns an empty report. The link is not checked per facility at ingest.

location_policy.crs_basis: EPA documents LATITUDE/LONGITUDE as the FRS value that best represents the facility, in decimal degrees. HORIZONTAL DATUM is blank for every RY2024 row, so the datum is not published. Coordinates are stored exactly as published and drawn as WGS 84 longitude/latitude without transformation (NAD83 and WGS 84 differ by about 1-2 m in the conterminous U.S.).
location_policy.source_quality_fields: none published in the basic file (no FRS collection method, accuracy, or reference point field)
rules: no_published_coordinates: LATITUDE and LONGITUDE both blank.
invalid_coordinates: only one of LATITUDE/LONGITUDE present, nonnumeric, nonfinite, outside latitude -90..90 or longitude -180..180, or exactly 0,0.
coarse_coordinate: LATITUDE or LONGITUDE published with at most two decimal places (about 1 km or coarser).
mapped: none of the above. Colocated facilities are all kept as separate points.
boundary_checks: within_published_state: the point lies in a TIGER/Line 2024 county of the state named in ST.
outside_published_state: the point lies in a TIGER/Line 2024 county of a different state. The point is still mapped; the published state and the spatially derived county are both kept.
outside_chip_boundary_layer: the point is not inside any CHIP 2024 county polygon (island areas AS, GU, MP, VI; offshore or shoreline points). Still mapped.
location_policy.never: No address is geocoded, no missing location is reconstructed, and no city, ZIP, or county centroid is substituted for a missing facility location. Facilities are never merged by address or coordinates.

boundary.vintage: TIGER/Line 2024 county equivalents (50 states, DC, Puerto Rico); used only for a spatial cross-check and a separately stored derived county

clustering.note: Clusters are display groupings of TRI reporting facilities in a fixed Web Mercator grid cell for the current zoom. They are not exposure zones, release footprints, or service areas.

interpretation: TRI covers facilities in covered industry sectors that meet EPA's employee and chemical-quantity thresholds for listed chemicals. Many sources of pollution are not required to report.
A facility's presence on this layer does not establish a regulatory violation and does not quantify health risk or exposure.
Absence from this layer does not establish the absence of pollution or of chemical use.
A reported chemical was manufactured, processed, or otherwise used above a TRI threshold. It is not necessarily released to air, or released at all.
Reporting for 2024 shows the facility filed TRI forms for that calendar year. It does not show that the facility is operating today.
limitations: Reporting year 2024 only, from EPA's national basic data file. EPA updates these files when facilities revise or withdraw forms; CHIP shows the reviewed snapshot named here.
Release and waste quantities are not shown in this phase. Form A certifications report no quantities (EPA fills zeroes), so zero must never be read as no release.
Facility locations are EPA FRS coordinates with no published datum or accuracy field. Facilities sharing a coordinate are listed separately, never merged.
The chemical filter lists facilities that filed at least one Form R or Form A for that TRI chemical ID. Trade-secret and mixture identities are EPA's generic labels.
Industry sector filters use the sector on each form; a facility appears under every sector it reported.
Clusters are display groupings only. CHIP does not calculate release totals, toxicity weights, exposure, risk, or distance zones.
usage_terms: EPA TRI basic data files are public U.S. Government data published by EPA's TRI Program; no use restriction is stated on the download page.

refresh_policy.new_reporting_year: requires a reviewed registry change (reporting_year, source URL, header, vocabularies)
